title: Variant compatibility matrix and fallback heuristics for hardware performance profiles
creator: Amina Desai
description: Background: As we onboard new model versions we publish hardware-specific performance profiles (A100/H100/L40S/MI300). Current profiles are per-variant but we lack a deterministic, auditable compatibility matrix and automated fallback rules when a pinned variant is unavailable or unstable. Objective: Produce a compatibility matrix and deterministic fallback heuristics that the routing layer and release playbooks can consume. Deliverables: 1) A CSV/JSON compatibility matrix mapping model flavors (fp16, int8, q4f16, q5_k_v) and sequence-length buckets to recommended device variants and profile pins; 2) A deterministic fallback heuristic spec (priority, max-latency multipliers, cost budget caps) for runtime routing; 3) A publishing/playbook update for the profile-publisher service to emit compatibility metadata and stability signatures; 4) Canary and repro workflows + telemetry thresholds for auto-repin recommendations.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility matrix file exists in model-onboard repo and is validated by unit tests
Runtime can query compatibility metadata and produce the same route decisions as the spec in >99% of synthetic requests
Fallback heuristic handles three failure modes: device OOM/slow, degraded kernel performance, capacity churn
Profile-publisher emits a stability_signature metric per variant and a compatibility_version tag
Runbook updated with explicit canary steps and manual reversion triggers
tests: Create synthetic workload suite with short/medium/long sequences and run against each device variant; assert latency P95 and token-cost deviations against baseline
Inject transient slowdowns (kernel slowdown simulation) in canary pool and assert routing falls back to next-priority variant within configured multiplier
Simulate capacity pressure by removing 30% of A100 pool and ensure requests respect cost caps and fallback to H100/L40S according to matrix
Verify the profile-publisher integration emits compatibility_version and stability_signature on publish; validate in CI that new publish increments semantic version
rollout_plan: 1) Merge compatibility matrix and heuristic spec under model-onboard/specs (feature branch) - ENG review
2) Profile-publisher PR to include compatibility metadata and bump publisher API (internal PR #) - limited to staging
3) Deploy routing change to staging with heuristic enabled behind feature flag - run regression suite
4) Canary: enable for 5% of production traffic, observe 48h telemetry (latency, errors, cost), postmortem and signoff
5) Gradual ramp to 100% over 3 days if canary green; if any metric breach follow runbook to rollback and collect traces
risks_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive fallbacks could increase unit cost significantly. Mitigation: introduce per-customer cost-budget caps and max fallback depth.
Risk: Compatibility matrix drift if kernel changes alter performance. Mitigation: include a stability_signature based on calibration runs and require re-certification when signature changes >2%

Risk: Mis-routed pinned customers get unexpected model quality. Mitigation: respect explicit customer pins (never override pinned model variant), only fallback variant selection for equivalent model-family variants.
Risk: Ambiguous ordering between H100 and L40S for certain seq-lengths. Mitigation: add tie-breaker rules based on cost-per-token and regional availability
telemetry_signatures: stability_signature: computed hash of perf-sample set + numeric stability_score (0-100)
latency_delta_pct: P95 delta compared to published profile baseline
cost_delta_pct: observed token-cost delta vs expected
route_switch_count: number of automatic fallbacks triggered per minute
